name: Sc2O3 bixbyite, 296 K
citation: H. Cong, H. Zhang, B. Yao, W. Yu, X. Zhao, J. Wang and G. Zhang. ScVO4: Explorations of Novel Crystalline Inorganic Optical Materials in Rare-Earth Orthovanadate Systems. Crystal Growth & Design 10 (2010), 4389-4400.
recommendation: recommended first-round source candidate; FEFF validation pending
method: Experimental single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Mo K-alpha (0.71073 angstrom), Bruker APEX2 CCD; full-matrix SHELXL-97 refinement with 308 reflections, 17 parameters, zero restraints, R1(observed)=0.0146. Sc and O coordinates and anisotropic displacement parameters are refined in the deposited CIF.
notes: Although the article title names ScVO4, its publisher abstract explicitly includes the obtained bixbyite-type Sc2O3 phase. This CIF is the separately refined Sc2O3 experimental structure, with formula O3 Sc2 and no V sites.
The paper combines experimental structures and ab initio calculations; this deposited CIF contains experimental diffraction/refinement metadata and is not a computed relaxation.

The article discusses high-temperature crystallization and vanadium-oxide vaporization; those formation conditions are not the diffraction temperature. Exact synthesis temperature for this particular Sc2O3 crystal is not verified and is left unspecified.
Measurement temperature is explicitly 296(2) K in both the cell and diffraction CIF tags; pressure is not specified.

All sites explicitly have occupancy 1. Symmetry expansion gives Sc 8b and 24d multiplicities 8 and 24; the CIF legacy multiplicity entries 6,2,1 are site-symmetry orders and must not be used as crystal population weights.
Both inequivalent Sc sites must be calculated and retained separately; site abundance weights are 1:3.

Selected in preference to COD1008928 (1953), whose original paper assumes oxygen positions from bixbyite packing, and COD9008121 (1967), whose listed 1968 erratum could not be inspected. Neither historical candidate is promoted.
